page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB per core memory allocation. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the c5.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests yield scores of 1494.09 and 7865.45 respectively, while Geekbench scores reach 1175.0 for single-core and 4531.0 for multi-core operations. Memory bandwidth tests show 437.77 GB/sec for cached small block reads and 50.41 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. The instance demonstrates average throughput in static web serving at 7.26 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 7.77 million operations per second.

Tradeoffs are evident in memory-intensive and large-scale AI workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, scoring 28.28 GB/sec. Large language model inference is a significant bottleneck; prompt processing for a medium 7B model is poor at 11.09 tokens/sec, and text generation is weak at 6.68 tokens/sec. Given these constraints and the lack of local storage, this instance is best suited for compute-bound workloads with moderate memory footprints, such as software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations, rather than large-scale LLM deployment or storage-heavy applications.
